Guaranteeing unobstructed access to third-party-developed source code is discharged by TDA-20.3's source-code escrow mechanism, made binding through TPM-05's contractual requirements on the provider.

The provider's contractual duty to report incidents is discharged by TPM-05.1's compelled compromise-notification agreements, and its duty to report on security posture by TPM-08's recurring provider review, both imposed via TPM-05 contract terms.

Requiring continuity measures at the provider's own site is discharged by BCD-10.3's contractual requirement that providers hold contingency plans meeting the organization's requirements, with TPM-11 covering joint response/recovery testing and BCD-01.2 the coordination of the two plan sets.

Compelling the provider to run controls at least as stringent as the bank's own is discharged by TPM-05's mechanism of imposing the organization's own security, compliance and resilience requirements contractually, with GOV-19.3 covering assurance of the provider's internal oversight.

Embedding a named baseline of security controls in the service agreement is TPM-05's contract-requirements mechanism, and extending it to the provider's subcontractors is TPM-05.2's contract flow-down mechanism.

Subjecting vendors to the bank's change management is discharged by CHG-02 and TPM-10 (control of supplier-initiated service changes), monitoring by TPM-08, and the separate obligation that service quality and availability to customers not degrade by OPS-03's service-management mechanism.

Multi-jurisdiction due diligence is discharged by TPM-04.1's pre-outsourcing risk assessment, the jurisdiction/data-location clause by TPM-04.4 and DCH-26's digital-sovereignty constraint mechanism, and contract termination on failure by TPM-05.7's break clauses.
mappings.uncovered_clause: A full exit strategy / transition-out plan, and the periodic re-review of jurisdictional information on significant change, have no discrete mechanism in the catalog.

mappings.rationale: Ensuring contracts do not obstruct audits and inspections is discharged by TPM-05's contractual requirements and CPL-03.3's mechanism for granting assessors the access needed to conduct a conformity assessment.
mappings.uncovered_clause: The duty to notify QCB as a priority when the bank's or the regulator's access rights are likely to be impeded.

mappings.rationale: As with 9.10.1.5, the subcontracting clause is a contract term (TPM-05) with flow-down of requirements to sub-contractors (TPM-05.2).
mappings.uncovered_clause: The bank's prior-approval gate for significant subcontracting is not a distinct catalog mechanism.

mappings.rationale: The compliance, audit and security content of the outsourcing agreement is discharged by TPM-05's contract-requirements mechanism and the contingency/DR/backup-facility content by BCD-10.3's contractually-required provider contingency plans, with OPS-03 covering service-management planning and support.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Quantified performance targets, service levels, reliability and scalability commitments have no dedicated SLA-definition mechanism in the catalog.

mappings.rationale: Requiring the provider to build a DR contingency framework with documented, maintained and tested plans is discharged by BCD-10.3 and TPM-11's joint response/recovery planning and testing, while the bank's own ability to keep operating through the disruption is discharged by BCD-02.2.

Periodic testing of the DR plan is discharged by BCD-04's contingency-plan tests and exercises, review and update by BCD-06's ongoing contingency planning, and identification of somewhere to resume IT operations by BCD-09's alternate processing site.
mappings.uncovered_clause: The exit-management plan and the identification of additional or alternate technology service providers.

mappings.rationale: Imposing equally stringent provider controls is TPM-05's contractual mechanism, periodic monitoring and review of those controls is TPM-08, and obtaining periodic expert reports on the provider's security adequacy is TPM-05.8's independent third-party attestation.

Preventing employee fraud is discharged through concrete personnel-control mechanisms: HRS-11's separation of duties to block unilateral inappropriate activity, THR-04's insider threat programme, and MON-16.1's monitoring of internal personnel activity.

Confining media holding account numbers, PINs, limits and balances to an authorized-personnel-only area is discharged by DCH-06.1's physical securing of sensitive media and PES-04.1's restriction of secure areas to authorized personnel, while the mandated physical separation of card production from PIN generation is discharged by PES-01.2's zone-based physical security.

Reporting ATM/POS fraud attempts, embezzlement, hacking and forged-card events to the MOI hotline and QCB is discharged by IRO-10's timely incident reporting to regulatory authorities, IRO-10.5's serious-incident reporting to relevant authorities, and IRO-14's maintained regulatory and law-enforcement contacts.

Securing cards, cheque books and internet passwords in courier transit is discharged by DCH-07's protection of media in transport outside controlled areas, DCH-07.1's named custodians throughout that transport, and NET-11's out-of-band physical delivery to the authorized individual.

Two-factor authentication and separate transaction credentials for internet banking are discharged by WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication, the multi-channel payee-registration step by IAC-02.4's out-of-band authentication, and the transaction value ceiling by DCH-25.1's transfer activity limits.
mappings.uncovered_clause: SMS alerting of customers on transactions has no dedicated customer-notification mechanism in the catalog.

mappings.rationale: Limiting information access to employees who need it to validate transactions is discharged by IAC-21's least privilege, IAC-08's role-based access enforcement, and DCH-03.1's restriction of sensitive-data disclosure to parties with a need to know.

The know-your-employee limb is discharged by HRS-04's pre-access personnel screening and the know-your-vendor limb by TPM-04.1's risk assessment before engaging a provider; IAC-28's identity verification covers only the identity-proofing part of customer onboarding.
mappings.uncovered_clause: KYC/AML customer due diligence as a financial-crime obligation is not a mechanism in the catalog.

mappings.rationale: Standing up a dedicated physical-infrastructure security team is an assignment-of-responsibility obligation, discharged by GOV-04's assignment of qualified individuals with mission and resources, operating the physical protection function that PES-01 governs.

Fraud-reporting channels are discharged by HRS-15's reprisal-free suspicious-activity reporting and IRO-11's reporting assistance to users, system triggers on exceptional transactions by DCH-25.1's anomalous-transaction identification, and detailed investigation by IRO-02's intake, analysis and containment handling.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Seeding and mystery-shopping detection exercises have no corresponding mechanism.

mappings.rationale: The well-publicized whistle-blowing mechanism is discharged by HRS-15's reprisal-free reporting channel, stakeholder disputes and exceptions by CPL-07's grievance intake and analysis, and the thorough investigation duty by IRO-02's incident analysis process.

A staffed email and phone channel for customers to report suspected fraud is discharged by IRO-11's mechanism for providing reporting assistance and advice to users, and training phone-banking and branch staff to handle those enquiries by SAT-03's role-based training.
mappings.uncovered_clause: The specific requirement for a dedicated email address and telephone number is an implementation detail no mechanism prescribes.

mappings.rationale: Computer forensics capability is discharged by IRO-08's digital forensics and chain-of-custody mechanism with IRO-08.1's licensed investigators, and large-volume data analysis tooling by MON-01.2's SIEM-based analysis capability.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Forensic accounting skills have no corresponding mechanism.

mappings.rationale: Reporting merchant-acquiring fraud to QCB is discharged by IRO-10's timely incident reporting to regulatory authorities, supported by IRO-14's maintained regulatory contacts.

Producing data and documents on police request is discharged by CPL-05's legal assessment of the investigative inquiry and CPL-05.2's provisioning of investigators with scoped access to support the official investigation.

Encouraging customers to report phishing emails and sites and acting on those reports is discharged by NET-20.9's mechanism for taking in user submissions of phishing attempts and using them to protect the organization.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Maintaining a customer-facing cyber security awareness and education programme; the catalog's awareness controls bind the workforce, not retail customers.

mappings.rationale: This obligation is itself programme-level - a security strategy for the confidentiality, integrity and availability of data and systems - which GOV-01's governance programme and OPS-02's documented plan for achieving security objectives discharge directly.

Adopting only cryptographic algorithms drawn from established, publicly scrutinised standards is exactly CRY-01's mechanism, with CRY-01.5 supplying the review of deployed cipher suites and WEB-10 the cryptographic delivery of the internet-facing systems being evaluated.

Two-factor transaction signing for online banking authorization is discharged by WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication for consumers, with IAC-02.4's out-of-band authentication supplying the independent second factor.

Authorizing institutional and corporate transactions with token-based mechanisms is discharged by WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication and IAC-02.4's out-of-band authentication, and the required risk assessment of those systems by RSK-04's recurring risk assessment.

Assuring customers that online login and transactions on the bank's website are protected and authenticated is discharged by WEB-10's cryptographic delivery of all web content, CRY-11's use of defined certificate authorities to establish protected sessions, and NET-09's protection of session authenticity and integrity.

Alerting on abnormal system activity and transmission errors is discharged by MON-01.12's automated alerting on anomalous activity, unusual online transactions by DCH-25.1's anomalous-transaction identification, and the action plan to verify and close issues by MON-17's analysis and triage tied into incident response.

Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of the online banking system is discharged by VPM-07's penetration testing, TDA-09.5's application-level penetration testing of the banking application itself, and VPM-06's routine vulnerability scanning.

Guarding online systems against DoS and DDoS is discharged by NET-02.1's denial-of-service protection and CAP-02's resource prioritisation for DoS-susceptible assets, while planning and tracking capacity utilisation is discharged by CAP-03's capacity planning and CAP-04's central monitoring of operating state and health.

Security measures for the bank's mobile online services and payments are discharged by WEB-04's controls protecting client data on client-facing services and WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication; the mobile-device-management controls are not applicable because the devices are the customers', not the bank's.

Protecting sensitive information used in mobile online services and payments is discharged by DCH-01.2's protection of sensitive data wherever processed or stored, CRY-03's cryptographic protection of that data in transmission, and WEB-04's client-data controls on the client-facing service.

The obligation is to educate retail customers on protecting their own personally-owned mobile devices from malware; the catalog's awareness and training mechanisms bind employees and contractors, and its mobile controls bind organization-managed devices, so no control discharges this.

Implementing 3D Secure for cardholder authentication is discharged by WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication for consumers, and the dedicated customer enrolment step by IAC-28's identity verification before issuing authenticators.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Informing customers about the authentication procedure has no corresponding customer-communication mechanism.

mappings.rationale: Compliance with named external payment and application security standards is discharged by CPL-01's identification and implementation of applicable contractual and regulatory controls and GOV-01.4's alignment of the programme with industry-recognized frameworks, with WEB-07 discharging the OWASP verification-standard limb specifically.

Annual reporting of standards compliance to QCB is discharged by GOV-17's mechanism for submitting programme status reporting to statutory and regulatory authorities, supported by CPL-01.5's declaration of conformity and CPL-01.3's ability to demonstrate conformity.

Withholding activation of a mailed payment card until the customer instructs it is related to IAC-28's verification of a user's identity before an authenticator is issued, but no control specifies an activation gate on a physically-delivered payment instrument.
mappings.uncovered_clause: The activation-on-customer-instruction gate itself.

mappings.rationale: OTP-based two-factor authentication for card-not-present internet transactions is discharged by WEB-06's Strong Customer Authentication, with IAC-02.4's out-of-band authentication supplying the one-time-password delivery channel.

Anti-skimming and tamper-resistant hardware on ATMs and kiosks is discharged by AST-07's protection of point-of-interaction devices from tampering and substitution and AST-08's periodic inspection for indicators of compromise, CCTV coverage by PES-05.1's surveillance-equipment monitoring, and PIN encryption on the pad and in transmission by CRY-03.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Physical measures to prevent shoulder-surfing of customer PINs.

mappings.rationale: Prohibiting merchants from retaining clear-text card data is discharged by TPM-05's imposition of security requirements in the merchant contract, DCH-13.3's protection requirements for sensitive data held on external parties' systems, and DCH-06.4's rendering of stored sensitive data human-unreadable.

Suppressing card details on merchant and customer receipts is discharged by DCH-03.2's masking of sensitive data that is displayed or printed, with DCH-03.1 restricting disclosure of that data to parties with a need to know.

Keeping account numbers, holder names and signatures on cheques in a secure area is discharged by DCH-06's secure storage of non-digital media within controlled areas, DCH-06.1's physical securing of all sensitive media, and PES-04.1's restriction of the secure area to authorized personnel.

Securing digitally signed cheques by cryptographic technique is discharged by CRY-08's PKI, which produces and validates the signatures, CRY-13's hash mechanism underpinning the integrity check, and CRY-09's management of the signing keys.

Reliability and resilience of core banking servers is discharged by SEA-01.2's achievement of resilience requirements in normal and adverse situations and BCD-12.2's near-real-time failover for critical assets, with NET-01's network security control procedures covering the cross-reference to network management guidelines.

Securing core banking applications is discharged by TDA-06's secure software development practices and securing the databases by CRY-05.3's database encryption, with DCH-01.2 covering protection of the sensitive data wherever it is processed or stored.

Vulnerability assessment and penetration testing of applications linked to the core banking system and its database is discharged by VPM-06's routine vulnerability scanning, VPM-07's penetration testing, and TDA-09.5's application-level penetration testing.
Adherence of core banking systems to cryptographic and key management guidelines is discharged by CRY-01's use of standards-based cryptographic protections and CRY-09's key management controls.

Core-system resilience is discharged by SEA-01.2's resilience requirements in adverse situations, archiving of security events for later analysis and legal retention by MON-10's retention of event logs against records-retention requirements, encryption of sensitive core database records by CRY-05.3, and restriction of core information to authorized users by IAC-08's role-based access control.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Integrity-control processes over the main core database data and the versioning system for application changes.

mappings.rationale: The clause states a regulator right, but the assessable duty falling on the bank is to be auditable by QCB on demand: grant the assessor logical and physical access (CPL-03.3) and be able to evidence conformity with the circular when asked (CPL-01.3). Deliberately not CPL-02.x (internal audit function) or CPL-04 (planning the organisation's own audits) - the mechanism here is supporting a supervisory examination, not running one. Nothing in SCF creates the regulator's power itself; that half is outside the assessed organisation.

Obligation is to educate the bank's retail customers via notifications and press releases. Every SCF awareness control is scoped to the workforce - SAT-02 to employees and contractors, SAT-03.x to internal roles, SAT-03.4 to vendors. Mapping to SAT-02 would be right domain, wrong audience and wrong mechanism. PRI-01.3 concerns publishing privacy-programme contact information, not security awareness campaigns.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Outbound security-awareness communication to banking customers (notifications, press releases) - SCF has no consumer-education control.

mappings.rationale: Binds the bank: a gate before signing any outsourcing agreement, plus submission of the outsourced scope to the supervisor. TPM-04.1 is the pre-acquisition assessment-and-approval gate that the QCB submission attaches to; GOV-06 is the documented regulator-contact channel through which approval is sought; TPM-01.1 maintains the provider/scope record that has to be submitted. SCF cannot supply the external approval decision itself.
mappings.uncovered_clause: QCB's prior written approval as a precondition to contract execution - an external regulatory consent, not an organisational mechanism.

mappings.rationale: Same bank-side duty as 9.10.1.2 without the scope-submission limb: no service-provider engagement may be contracted until approval is obtained, so the pre-contract approval gate (TPM-04.1) must include the supervisory step, exercised through the documented regulator contact channel (GOV-06). Avoided CPL-01 as an umbrella - the obligation is a specific procurement gate, not general regulatory-compliance identification.
mappings.uncovered_clause: The regulator's grant or refusal of prior approval.

mappings.rationale: Continuous fraud-risk education aimed at customers for their own protection. SCF's fraud-adjacent control (DCH-25.1) is a detection mechanism over anomalous transaction activity, not customer communication, and the SAT family is workforce-scoped. Forcing either would be a mechanism mismatch.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Ongoing fraud-awareness education delivered to customers.

mappings.rationale: Two limbs, both outside SCF's mechanism set: board/senior-management sponsorship of a consumer-education programme and resourcing of it. GOV-01.1 and GOV-04.1 concern executive oversight and accountability for the internal security programme, so using them here would be an umbrella substitution for a specific external-education obligation.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Governing-body commitment and resourcing for ongoing customer education initiatives.

mappings.rationale: Composite. The detection limb - identifying card withdrawals or charges that exceed defined thresholds as anomalous transaction activity to curb fraud - is discharged by DCH-25.1. The delivery limb is not: SCF has no control requiring a prompt alert to the cardholder carrying transaction source and amount, and MON-01.12 routes alerts to incident-response personnel, not to the account holder, so it would be the wrong recipient.
mappings.uncovered_clause: Prompt cardholder-facing transaction alerts, including source and amount, on customer-defined thresholds.

mappings.rationale: The obligation is regular awareness messaging to customers about ATM tampering indicators. AST-07 (protecting point-of-interaction devices from tampering and substitution) and AST-08 (periodic inspection for indicators of compromise) address the same threat but discharge it through the bank inspecting and hardening its own ATMs - a different mechanism from telling customers what to look for, so mapping them would be right domain, wrong mechanism.
